function.name: file_edit
function.description: Surgically edit an existing file in place under an atomic per-file lock. Preferred usage: (1) pass `target` (exact existing text to replace, without line numbers) and `replacement` (new text), optionally scoped with 1-indexed `start_line` and `end_line` from file_read; (2) pass `start_line`, `end_line`, and `replacement` to directly replace that inclusive line range without echoing a large `target` block; (3) for multiple independent changes in the same file in a single atomic call, pass `edits`: [{"target": "...", "replacement": "...", "start_line": 10, "end_line": 15}, ...] (multi-hunk line ranges are applied bottom-up automatically so top-down line numbers from file_read never drift); or (4) legacy `expression` with `<<<<<<< SEARCH ... ======= ... >>>>>>> REPLACE` blocks. Features a 4-tier fuzzy matcher (exact -> line-number strip -> whitespace/indentation normalization -> smart-quote/dash typography normalization) and returns closest-match line numbers if a target block is not found. You can also emit multiple `file_edit` calls across different files in a single turn for parallel execution. Edits that break shell syntax (bash -n) are automatically reverted.

path.description: Target file path relative to workspace root (e.g. "lib/core/react.sh", "web/src/main.rs").

target.description: Exact existing lines/text in the file to search for and replace (do not include 'NN: ' line-number prefixes). Optional when both `start_line` and `end_line` are provided.

replacement.description: New text to replace `target` (or lines `start_line`..`end_line`) with (use empty string "" to delete).

start_line.description: Optional 1-indexed starting line number (inclusive) from `file_read` to scope `target` matching or replace lines `start_line`..`end_line` directly.

end_line.description: Optional 1-indexed ending line number (inclusive) from `file_read` to scope `target` matching or replace lines `start_line`..`end_line` directly.

edits.description: Optional array of multiple surgical edits [{"target": "...", "replacement": "...", "start_line": 10, "end_line": 15}] to apply atomically to this file in a single call.

target.description: Exact existing lines/text to replace (optional when `start_line` and `end_line` are provided).

replace_all.description: If true, replace all occurrences of target (default: false).
If true, replace all occurrences of `target` in the file instead of requiring a unique match (default: false).

expression.description: Legacy fallback: <<<<<<< SEARCH ... ======= ... >>>>>>> REPLACE block(s). Prefer `target` + `replacement` or `edits` instead.

function.name: crypto_standing_order
function.description: Standing orders are price-corridor traps: the operator pre-approves Tier B buys for one strategy and asset within an ADA cap and price band until an expiry. Multi-corridor ladders are supported: non-overlapping [price_min, price_max] corridors on the same asset coexist as an active ladder up to the asset's position cap (e.g. 95% of working capital), and coexist with Gate-1 'live' S2 signal buys on a First-Trigger-Wins basis. Overlapping corridors (or passing supersede_so_id / replace=true) atomically supersede the overlapping/targeted order. While active, the signal scan evaluates rungs from shallowest to deepest and places the buy when spot dips into a rung's band (after a 90s falling-knife stabilization check); if that buy does not fill within no_fill_hours it is reclaimed and that rung's capacity re-arms. action='create' builds a Tier B plan that the operator must confirm (pass: action, strategy, asset, max_ada, price_min, price_max, expires_hours, no_fill_hours; optional: supersede_so_id, replace, reason; NEVER pass id on create); 'list' shows active ones; 'revoke' cancels one immediately by id ('SO-XXXXXX').
